material_findings.title: xTech|Search 10 exposes phase-level awards but retains an eligibility conflict
material_findings.summary: Current Army and USA.gov surfaces agree that xTech|Search 10 is open Sep. 10-Oct. 19, 2026 with up to $1M in cash prizes. The Army page now exposes $5K semifinalist, $20K finalist, $200K/$100K/$50K final awards, plus up to 20 Phase I SBIR/STTR proposals at up to $300K each, but the same page contains conflicting statements about who can submit.
material_findings.eligibility_and_cost: Detailed Army eligibility text says small, for-profit, independent U.S. businesses with no more than 500 employees, while the footer says small and large U.S.-based and allied foreign-country businesses. USA.gov says eligible small businesses around the U.S. No entry fee was identified. Full RFI controls eligibility and must be preserved before case promotion.
material_findings.prize_and_deadline_evidence: Army: Phase 1 up to 50 semifinalists at $5K each; Phase 2 up to 20 finalists at $20K each; Phase 3 first/second/third at $200K/$100K/$50K; Phase 4 up to 20 SBIR/STTR selectees at up to $300K each. Application deadline is Oct. 19, 2026 at 5 PM ET. USA.gov independently lists a $1M cash-prize headline and the same opening/closing dates.
material_findings.scope_and_safety: This is an innovation/prize opportunity, not authorization to test Army or government systems. Any security-related concept would still require a competition-defined problem and data/test environment.
material_findings.recommended_action: When chronology reaches this contribution, preserve and review the full RFI to resolve eligibility, ownership, prior-support, submission, IP/data-rights and judging terms before creating active participant-specific work.
